title: 9-8-8: Suicide Crisis Helpline
organization: Centre for Addiction and Mental Health (CAMH), funded by the Government of Canada
label: Crisis support
note: Canada's national suicide crisis helpline. Call or text 9-8-8, 24 hours a day, every day of the year, in English and French. Led by CAMH and funded by the Government of Canada. Checked on 23 September 2026.

title: Kids Help Phone
label: Crisis support
note: Free 24/7 support for young people aged 5 to 29 (age range from the Government of Canada page). Call 1-800-668-6868 or text CONNECT to 686868. Calls are confidential and anonymous. Texting is confidential but not anonymous, and staff may contact emergency services if someone's safety is at risk. Checked on 23 September 2026.

title: Hope for Wellness Help Line
label: Crisis support
note: 24/7 counselling and crisis support for First Nations, Inuit and Métis people across Canada. Call 1-855-242-3310. Checked on 23 September 2026.

title: 211 Ontario
label: Service navigation
note: Help finding non-emergency community, social and health services in Ontario. Call or text 2-1-1, or call 1-877-330-3213, 24/7 in more than 150 languages. For emergencies it tells people to call 9-1-1. Checked on 23 September 2026.

title: ConnexOntario
label: Service navigation
note: Free 24/7 help finding mental health, addiction and problem gambling services in Ontario. Call 1-866-531-2600 or text CONNEX to 247247. Funded by the Government of Ontario and Ontario Health. Checked on 23 September 2026.

title: Sakeenah Canada emergency hotline
label: Women's services
note: Supports women and children leaving domestic violence, homelessness and poverty, with homes in several Canadian cities. Its 24/7 emergency hotline is 1-888-671-3446 (confirmed on https://sakeenahcanada.com/service/emergency-hotline/). The hotline page also says to call 9-1-1 in immediate danger. Checked on 23 September 2026.

title: Nisa Helpline
label: Women's services
note: Free, confidential peer support for Muslim women and girls aged 14 and up. Call +1 888 711 6472, 7 days a week, 8 AM to midnight Eastern time. It is peer support, not a crisis line. The same page's FAQ still shows an older number (1-888-315-6472); the header number was used. nisahelpline.org is now a parking page and is not linked. Checked on 23 September 2026.

title: Nisa Homes
label: Women's services
note: Nisa Homes is a Nisa Foundation program offering safe shelter for women and children, with locations across Canada. Apply through the Nisa Foundation site or call the helpline, +1 888 711 6472. nisahomes.com could not be opened, so it is not linked. Checked on 23 September 2026.

title: LaunchGood Zakat Policy
label: Financial education

title: Workplace accommodation: A guide for federally regulated workplaces
label: Public rights source
note: Supports the federal route: the Canadian Human Rights Act covers federally regulated employers such as federal departments, First Nations governments, banks, Crown corporations like Canada Post, broadcasting, and air and rail transport. Religion is a protected ground, with modified hours for religious practice as an example. Four steps (conversation, assess, accommodate, review), a written plan signed by everyone, and complaints within one year of the last discriminatory act. Page dated 2026-03-23.

title: Policy on preventing discrimination based on creed, section 9: The duty to accommodate
label: Public rights source
note: Supports the Ontario duty to accommodate sincerely held creed practices to the point of undue hardship, the sincerity test (no need to prove a practice is essential), the three undue hardship factors (cost, outside funding, health and safety), the requester's part (reasonable notice, answering questions, taking part), and the prayer-space dignity example. General information, not legal advice.

title: Policy on preventing discrimination based on creed, section 10: Specific cases
label: Public rights source
note: Supports the Ontario examples: prayer times that move with the sun, flexible breaks or staggered hours, no loss of pay for insignificant prayer time, working through lunch in Ramadan to leave early, and religious holidays without being forced to use vacation days. Section 10.2 (dress code and appearance): employers must accommodate a religious beard or head covering short of undue hardship, with a bearded, turbaned Sikh security guard as the example; it also quotes York Region District School Board guidelines on phys-ed clothing, private changing and alternative swimwear. Section 10.5 (creed-based exemptions): a Newfoundland case where a tribunal found an employer should have let someone else sell tickets to an event with alcohol instead of suspending a Pentecostal employee. Section 10.6 (food): creed-based food restrictions can extend to handling food, with a plant that reassigned employees who could not handle pork. Rechecked 25 September 2026.

title: Duty to accommodate at work
label: Public rights source
note: Supports that Alberta lists religious beliefs as a protected ground that employers must accommodate at work.

title: Personal characteristics protected in the BC Human Rights Code
sourceType: Official provincial human rights tribunal page
label: Public rights source
note: Supports that religion is a protected characteristic under the BC Human Rights Code.

title: Act respecting the laicity of the State (chapter L-0.3), consolidated to 1 September 2026
label: Public rights source
note: Supports the Quebec box: s. 6 and Schedule II (religious symbol ban for listed roles, including teachers and principals in school service centres, peace officers, school staff in contact with students and subsidised childcare staff), s. 10.1 (religious practice prohibited in places under listed public bodies, with exceptions), Schedule I para 7 (colleges and universities), s. 10.3 (overt prayer in subsidised private schools during instructional hours) and s. 34 (notwithstanding clause). Needs legal review before it is relied on.

title: Bill 9, An Act respecting the reinforcement of laicity in Quebec
label: Public rights source
note: Supports the dates: introduced 27 November 2025, passed and assented to on 2 April 2026 as Statutes of Quebec 2026, chapter 6, in force 2 April 2026 with exceptions. Held for legal review.

title: Know Your Rights and Responsibilities: A Guide for Canadian Muslims
label: Public rights source
note: Supports the list of accommodations a Muslim employee can ask for in Canada: prayer time and space, storing a prayer mat, time for wudu, Jumu'ah, fasting, holidays, dress, and not handling pork or alcohol. Dated March 2019 (PDF metadata), so some parts may be out of date. Not legal advice.

title: Managers Guide to supporting Muslim Employees
organization: Muslim Federal Employees Network (hosted by APEX)
label: Public rights source
note: Supports the practical prayer details: up to three of the five prayers can fall in a 9 to 5 workday, each prayer break typically takes 10 to 15 minutes, wudu can be done in a public washroom, a clean quiet private space works, employees bring their own mat, and Jumu'ah needs at least an hour. A network's job aid, not official Government of Canada policy.

title: Seven Days, Seven Verses: Living the Message of Al-Fatihah
label: Learning resource

label: Learning resource
note: Live online small-group recitation classes (Al-Fatihah, Al-Kauthar, Al-Ikhlas, An-Nas), sessions segregated by gender, ten slots between 6:00 and 9:30 pm Eastern. NMA states its courses are free. The site loads Google Analytics and a Facebook pixel. Partially verified.

label: Learning resource

title: Qur'an 30 for 30: Thematic Tafsir
label: Learning resource

label: Learning resource

title: List of charities and other qualified donees
label: Official source

title: Quran 2:184 - Making up fasts and fidyah
label: Quran source
note: Translation of meaning (The Clear Quran): whoever is ill or on a journey fasts an equal number of days after Ramadan; those who can only fast with extreme difficulty may compensate by feeding a needy person for every day not fasted. The English is a translation of the meaning.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 1933 - Eating or drinking by mistake while fasting
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih al-Bukhari: whoever forgets and eats or drinks while fasting should complete the fast, because Allah fed them and gave them drink. Checked on Sunnah.com.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 1923 - Blessing in suhoor
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih al-Bukhari: 'Take Suhur as there is a blessing in it.' Checked on Sunnah.com.

title: Sunan Abi Dawud 2356 - Breaking the fast with dates or water
label: Hadith reference
note: The Prophet (peace be upon him) broke his fast with fresh dates, or dry dates, or water. Grade shown on Sunnah.com: Hasan Sahih (Al-Albani).

title: How Does Ramadan Work? A Beginner's Guide
label: Research education
note: Guest author, published 8 March 2024, updated 7 September 2026. Covers the fast from dawn to sunset, forgetful eating, tarawih, the last ten nights, zakat al-fitr (about 3 kg of staple food, before the Eid prayer), and the illness and travel exemptions with make-up days. Its footnotes were not all checked.

title: The Complete Guide to Fasting
label: Scholar education
note: By Ustadha Naielah Ackbarali, 9 August 2010, following the Hanafi school: what invalidates the fast and whether it needs a make-up only or a make-up plus expiation (kaffarah), the exemptions, and making up fasts after Ramadan. Other schools differ on some details.

title: Donate wisely and avoid fraud
label: Public safety source
note: Supports checking a charity on the CRA lists, paying the charity rather than an individual, and not giving under pressure; lists red flags such as cash, gift cards, couriers and free email addresses. Last updated 2 September 2025.

title: Charity and donation fraud
label: Public safety source
note: Supports refusing high-pressure requests, asking for a charity's registration number and checking it with the CRA (1-800-267-2384), asking for information in writing, and watching for false crowdfunding ads, including for religious causes. Modified 15 January 2026.

title: Nisab value: what is nisab?
label: Financial education
note: Nisab as 87.48 g of gold or 612.36 g of silver; the charity uses silver so more people pay and more are helped, or gold if gold is your only asset; hawl of one lunar year (354 days); 2.5 percent, or 2.577 percent on a Gregorian year (companion zakat page). Footer: Registered Charity No. 821896875RR0001. Dollar values on the page change with metal prices and are not repeated here.

title: Fidya
label: Financial education
note: Fidya is for someone who cannot fast for a lasting valid reason and cannot make the days up: feed one person per missed fast. Kaffarah, for a fast broken without a valid reason, means feeding 60 people per fast. The 2026 amount is CAD 15 per missed fast. Cites Quran 2:184 and notes many scholars include pregnancy. Reviewed September 2026.

title: How do I calculate zakat on my retirement savings, RRSP and TFSA?
label: Financial education
note: NZF Canada's method: count RRSP or TFSA funds you can access at their value on your zakat date; for an RRSP you may deduct the withholding tax (10, 20 or 30 percent; 5, 10 or 15 percent in Quebec). Its calculator uses 85 g of gold or 595 g of silver. Footer: Registered Charity No. 839912599RR0001.

title: Zakat policy
label: Financial education
note: States an administration cap of one eighth (12.5 percent), distribution within one lunar year, named zakat advisors, and that it reads the category of those whose hearts are to be reconciled as including new converts. Reviewed January 2026. Shown on the page: CRA no. 827502741 RR0001. Its category list omits freeing captives, which Quran 9:60 names.

title: Zakat calculator
label: Financial education
note: Calculator using a gold nisab of 88 g by default, with silver at 613 g as an option (its explanatory text gives 87.49 g and 613.35 g); counts only the coming year's principal on long-term debts; notes the difference of opinion on worn jewellery. Names Mufti Yusuf Badat as Zakat Policy Advisor. Shown on the page: CRA Charity No. 89733-1732-RR0001. The price feed may be out of date.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 6464: the most beloved deeds are the regular ones
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih al-Bukhari: the most beloved deed to Allah is the most regular and constant, even if it is little. Checked on Sunnah.com.

label: Official resource

label: Publisher source

title: Elements of Effective Practice for Mentoring: mentor preparation and training
label: Program benchmark

label: Program benchmark

label: Training material

title: Police record checks
label: Public safety information
note: Explains Ontario's three types of police record check, what each discloses, and when a vulnerable sector check can be asked for.

label: App documentation

label: Official app

Shafi'i: a learner may read Al-Fatihah from a mushaf in prayer; a translation is not allowed. Maliki and Hanbali: recitation in another language is not valid. Learn Al-Fatihah gradually. Link only.

label: Scholarly answer

label: Hadith reference
note: Sahih al-Bukhari 5167 (sahih by collection). Supports: Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf gave gold the weight of a date stone as mahr, and the Prophet told him 'Give a banquet, even if with one sheep.'

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 5090: marry for religion
label: Hadith reference
note: Sahih al-Bukhari 5090 (sahih by collection). Supports: a woman is married for four things, and the Prophet advised choosing the one with religion. It does not mention ethnicity.

title: Marriage when bride has no wali / guardian (AMJA fatwa 87635)
organization: Assembly of Muslim Jurists of America (AMJA)
label: Scholar answer
note: Dr. Hatem al-Haj, 24 October 2012. Supports: a marriage a woman contracts herself is valid according to Abu Hanifah, while the other schools require a guardian; the masjid imam can act for a new Muslim woman with no Muslim family, and repeating the contract with the imam acting for her is advised.

title: How can I have a nikah without announcing my conversion to family?
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadha Shazia Ahmad, checked by Shaykh Irshaad Sedick, 4 April 2025. Supports: a convert does not need her non-Muslim father's permission; the witnesses are two Muslim men or one man and two women (the answer names no school); secret marriages are discouraged; her teacher recommended converts be Muslim for about a year before marrying (a recommendation, not a ruling).

title: Meeting a potential spouse through school or work?
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadha Zaynab Ansari Abdul-Razacq, November 2009. Supports: converts often lack family networks and meet a spouse at school or work; meetings should be chaperoned; no secret relationships; a guardian may refuse an unsuitable match.

title: Getting married
label: Public rights source
note: Page updated 2 September 2026. Supports, for Ontario: a marriage licence or banns; a religious officiant must be duly recognised by their religious body; the couple, two witnesses and the officiant sign right after the ceremony; age 18, or 16 to 17 with written parental consent.

title: Rules on marriage ceremonies in Quebec
label: Public rights source
note: Supports, for Quebec: the officiant must be authorised by law; at least two witnesses; a notice is published on the Directeur de l'etat civil site at least 20 days before the marriage; the ceremony can be civil or religious.

title: Marriage
label: Public rights source
note: Supports, for British Columbia: anyone performing a marriage must be registered with the Vital Statistics Agency; a marriage licence is needed; the couple, two witnesses and the officiant sign.

title: Getting married
label: Public rights source
note: Supports, for Alberta: religious officiants must be registered with Vital Statistics; a valid Alberta marriage licence is always needed; two witnesses attend.

title: Enforceability of mahr under a shari'a law-based contract in New Zealand: a comparison with United Kingdom, Australia, and Canada
organization: Durgeshree Raman, International Journal of Law, Policy and the Family 38(1), 2024
label: Research source
note: Peer-reviewed article. Its Canada section summarises courts that enforced a mahr agreement (Nathoo v Nathoo and Amlani v Hirani in British Columbia, Khanis v Noormohamed in Ontario), an Ontario court that declined (Kaddoura v Hammoud), and the Supreme Court's view in Bruker v Marcovitz that a religious undertaking meeting contract rules can be enforced. A secondary summary; the judgments themselves were not opened.

title: Divorce and conversion to Islam
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Abdurragmaan Khan, 18 September 2019 (Shafi'i fiqh). Supports: a man's marriage to his Christian wife stays valid after he becomes Muslim. Its footnote adds that in the strict Shafi'i school this holds only if she is of Israelite descent or her forebears became Christian before the Council of Nicaea; other schools do not require this.

title: Can you advise me on how to convert as a 13-year-old?
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadha Shazia Ahmad, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 28 April 2023. Supports: a teenager's Shahada is valid and is all it takes; 'For now, don't worry about being unable to cover, fast, or attend a mosque'; take every chance to practise you get; learn online and make dua.

title: Dealing with non-Muslim parents (II)
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadh Faraz A. Khan, 11 August 2010. Supports: love and excellent conduct toward parents who are not Muslim; obedience is limited only by 'There is no obedience to creation if it entails disobedience to the Creator' (Tabarani).

title: Leaving home
label: Public rights source
note: A Legal Aid Ontario-funded legal clinic for young people, not a government page. Supports, for Ontario: at 15 and under, parents or caregivers decide where a young person lives; at 16 or 17 a young person may withdraw from parental control without a court order; routes through a Children's Aid Society; a person a youth lives with will not be charged with a criminal offence as long as they do not help the youth leave home.

title: Quran 66:6: Protect yourselves and your families
label: Quran source
note: Supports: believers are told to protect themselves and their families from a Fire. The English wording is a translation of the meaning, checked against The Clear Quran (Dr. Mustafa Khattab).

title: How can I ensure my child gets proper Islam despite my ex-spouse?
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadha Shazia Ahmad, checked by Shaykh Irshaad Sedick, 26 January 2025. Supports: keep talking with the co-parent, pray and practise during your time with the child, arrange a Quran teacher, keep Islamic manners with mercy, and make dua.

title: Divorce Act, section 16: best interests of the child
organization: Government of Canada, Justice Laws Website
label: Public rights source
note: Current to 3 September 2026. Supports: only the child's best interests are considered; primary consideration goes to the child's physical, emotional and psychological safety; factors include the child's views, given due weight for age and maturity (s. 16(3)(e)), and the child's cultural, linguistic, religious and spiritual upbringing and heritage (s. 16(3)(f)).

title: Best interests of the child: the Divorce Act changes explained
label: Public rights source
note: Page modified 17 May 2024. Supports: religion may give a child an added support system, and a parent's ability to keep the child's link to their religious heritage may matter; the weight depends on the child.

title: Policy/Program Memorandum 162: exemption from instruction related to human development and sexual health
label: Public rights source
note: Issued 21 August 2019. Supports, for Ontario: school boards must allow parents to request an exemption for their child from the Grades 1 to 8 Human Development and Sexual Health expectations; parents are told at least 20 school days before that instruction; a standard exemption form is used every school year.

title: Quran 17:23 to 24: Kindness to parents in old age
label: Quran source
note: Supports: honour parents, especially in old age; do not say even a word of impatience; lower the wing of humility out of mercy and pray for mercy on them. The English wording is a translation of the meaning, checked against The Clear Quran (Dr. Mustafa Khattab).

title: My husband does not allow me to support my non-Muslim mother. What do I do?
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadha Raidah Shah Idil, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 21 February 2017. Supports: she is obligated to look after her mother and keep family ties; she is advised to set aside money each month from her own earnings as charity (sadaqah) and to visit weekly. It states no fiqh ruling that financial support of a non-Muslim parent is obligatory.

title: Is it permissible to help a non-Muslim practice their faith?
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadh Farid Dingle, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 21 February 2021. Supports: directly facilitating another religion's rites is not permissible (examples: holding a baby for baptism, charity to a temple); indirect help, such as telling someone where a church is, is not sinful.

title: Transporting non Muslim parents to church
organization: Darul Uloom Trinidad and Tobago (on IslamQA.org)
label: Scholar answer
note: Mufti Waseem Khan, Hanafi, undated. Supports: it is better not to be the means of taking a parent to church, but it is not sinful when the parent has no one else to take them.

title: Can I Work for a Restaurant Serving Pork and Alcohol?
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadh Salman Younas (Hanafi), checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 6 September 2016. Supports: serving pork and alcohol is not permissible; if leaving at once would cause serious hardship, such as not meeting rent and basic needs, one may keep working while actively looking for a permissible job. One Hanafi answer.

title: Can I Work at an Establishment That Sells Haram Food?
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Yusuf Weltch (Hanafi), checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 7 November 2020. Supports: directly preparing or promoting haram food is not permissible (citing Quran 5:2); an indirect role such as cashier is permissible; caution suggests looking for other work.

title: Can I Work in a Restaurant That Sells Alcohol?
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadh Salman Younas, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 17 September 2016. Supports: a cleaning (porter) job in a restaurant that sells alcohol, and its income, are permissible because the worker is not directly helping in sin.

title: Working in an interest-based bank when some of its activities are halal (AMJA fatwa 22421)
organization: Assembly of Muslim Jurists of America (AMJA)
label: Scholar answer
note: Dr. Salah Al-Sawy, 23 August 2007. Supports: working directly in interest-based credit is not permissible; other banking services are lawful in principle; advises an earnest search for other permissible work.

title: Selling alcohol (AMJA fatwa 23386)
organization: Assembly of Muslim Jurists of America (AMJA)
label: Scholar answer
note: Dr. Salah Al-Sawy, 26 July 2008. Supports: selling alcohol is prohibited by consensus. The consensus wording covers selling alcohol only.

title: Jami at-Tirmidhi 1295: Ten people cursed in connection with wine
label: Hadith reference
note: Jami at-Tirmidhi 1295, graded hasan (Darussalam); at-Tirmidhi calls this route through Anas gharib. Cited for: the one who serves wine and the one who sells it are among the ten cursed.

title: Quran 5:2: Cooperate in goodness, not in sin
label: Quran source
note: Cited for: cooperate with one another in goodness and righteousness, and do not cooperate in sin and transgression. The English wording is a translation of the meaning, checked against The Clear Quran.

title: Jami at-Tirmidhi 2165: The third of them is Shaytan
label: Hadith reference
note: Jami at-Tirmidhi 2165, graded sahih (Darussalam), within Umar's sermon at al-Jabiyah. Cited for: a man is not alone with a woman except that the third of them is Shaytan.

title: Seclusion in the Office
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadh Tabraze Azam (Hanafi, citing Radd al-Muhtar), checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 6 December 2018. Supports: an office people routinely enter, or one with a window or a third person, is not prohibited seclusion (khalwa); at lunch breaks and quiet times keep the door open or step away.

title: What Is the Meaning of Khalwa (Seclusion) with the Opposite Gender?
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadh Salman Younas (Hanafi), checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 23 May 2015. Supports: khalwa is physical seclusion in an enclosed place others cannot see into or enter; private communication in professional and educational settings is permissible and is not seclusion; flirtatious chat and dating sites are not permissible.

title: Guidelines for Interacting With the Opposite Sex
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadha Zaynab Ansari, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 29 December 2010 (no school named). Supports: talking to or working with a member of the opposite sex when there is a need is fine; lower the gaze; avoid khalwa (it says one man with two women is not khalwa, which some Hanafi answers read differently); men cover from navel to knee and women all but the face and hands.

title: Can We Play Video Games Online with the Opposite Gender?
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadha Shazia Ahmad (Shafi'i), 31 July 2022. Supports: any unnecessary activity with the opposite gender, including online gaming and chat, is 'undoubtedly inappropriate', because online settings lower inhibitions.

title: Quran 24:30-31: Lowering the gaze and covering
label: Quran source
note: Cited for: believing men and believing women are told to lower their gaze and guard their chastity, and women to draw their head coverings over their chests and not show their adornment except to the people the verse lists. The English wording is a translation of the meaning, checked against The Clear Quran.

title: What is Considered Awra (Nakedness) for Men?
label: Scholar answer
note: SeekersGuidance Answers Service, approved by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani (Hanafi, citing Ascent to Felicity), 14 March 2011. Supports: a man's awrah is from the navel to the knee, with the navel not included and the knee included; it is covered at all times unless there is a need.

title: Covering Nakedness While Swimming
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadha Shazia Ahmad, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 7 November 2020. Supports: a man must cover from the navel to the knees and a little beyond while swimming; suggests three-quarter compression pants.

title: Is Swimming Permissible for Women in Islam?
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Anas al-Musa, 4 October 2025. Supports: swimming is permissible for women with conditions: women-only places preferred, loose clothing that is not thin, and avoiding public changing rooms. It also says a married woman needs her husband's permission and cites a hadith against removing clothes outside the home.

title: Quran 33:59: Drawing the outer garment
label: Quran source
note: Cited for: the Prophet is told to tell his wives, daughters and the believing women to draw their cloaks over their bodies, so they are recognised as virtuous and not harassed. The English wording is a translation of the meaning, checked against The Clear Quran.

title: How To Start Wearing a Hijab?
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadha Shazia Ahmad, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 12 October 2023. Supports: advises starting right away rather than in small stages, with a simple style; cites Quran 33:59; any style is fine if the hair, neck and head are covered.

title: Should I Wear the Hijab Despite the Difficulty to Get a Job Wearing It?
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadha Shireen Ahmed, 24 September 2017 (no 'checked by' line on the page). Supports: the four schools hold hijab obligatory; mentions many hijab-wearing women doctors in Toronto.

title: Sahih Muslim 258: The forty-night limit for grooming
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih Muslim. Cited for: a time limit was set for trimming the moustache, cutting the nails, removing underarm hair and shaving pubic hair, that they not be left for more than forty nights.

title: Sahih Muslim 261a: Ten acts of the fitrah
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih Muslim. Cited for: the ten acts of the fitrah: trimming the moustache, letting the beard grow, the tooth-stick, rinsing the nose, cutting the nails, washing the finger joints, removing underarm hair, shaving pubic hair, washing the private parts with water, and a tenth the narrator forgot, possibly rinsing the mouth.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 5892: Let the beard grow, cut the moustache short
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih al-Bukhari. Cited for: 'keep the beards and cut the moustaches short'; Ibn Umar trimmed what went past his fist at Hajj or Umrah.

title: What is the Ruling of Shaving and Shortening the Beard in the Shafi'i School?
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Amjad Rasheed (Shafi'i), 25 November 2016. Supports: the relied-upon Shafi'i position (al-Rafi'i and al-Nawawi) is that a full beard is recommended and shaving is disliked, not unlawful; the majority of scholars hold complete shaving unlawful; scholars agree shaving without an excuse is blameworthy.

title: What Is a Beard in the Hanafi School?
label: Scholar answer
note: Mawlana Ilyas Patel (Hanafi), checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 20 October 2023. Supports: in the Hanafi school keeping the beard is wajib, a fistful is the standard, and shaving is prohibited. It also gives the Maliki view (al-Dasuqi: shaving is unlawful) and the Shafi'i view. The Hanbali view is not covered.

title: Policy on Scheduling of Classes and Examinations and Other Accommodations for Religious Observances
label: Official source
note: Policy dated 29 June 2005. Supports: students alert instructors in good time; instructors avoid scheduling tests on holy days; students get the chance to make up missed work and write at an alternate time; no student should be seriously disadvantaged. General information, not legal advice.

title: Religious accommodation support
label: Official source
note: Supports: documentation from faith leaders is not required; the Multi-Faith Centre is at 569 Spadina Crescent.

title: Academic Accommodation for all Students' Religious Observances and for the Cultural Observances of First Nations, Metis, and Inuit Students
organization: University of British Columbia (Vancouver Academic Calendar)
label: Official source
note: Live UBC Calendar page (Senate policy J-136), checked 25 September 2026. Supports: documentation from faith or community leaders is not required; students request accommodation with as much notice as possible (normally 14 days); observance may require temporary absence for daily prayers, fasting or breaking a fast, or following dress codes; accommodations include an alternative exam date.

title: Praying on a Plane
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Faraz Rabbani (Hanafi), 14 August 2009. Supports: the obligatory prayer must be prayed on a plane when its time comes in; stand, or sit with a real prostration, when reasonably possible; estimate the prayer times. Whether a seated prayer must be repeated later differs between schools and is not covered here.

title: Pearson Chapel, Terminal 1
label: Official travel source
note: Supports: the Terminal 1 chapel is before security on Level 1 Arrivals, open to anyone at Pearson and interdenominational. It does not mention a separate Muslim prayer room.

title: How Can a Newly Muslim Convert Handle Difficulty Finding Halal Meat?
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Yusuf Weltch, checked by Shaykh Abdul-Rahim Reasat, 28 September 2024. Supports: legitimate kosher meat (with God's name mentioned) is permissible in the Hanafi school; eating pescatarian for a while is an option; no need to investigate hypothetical cross-contamination, with fried food the main thing to ask about.

title: Is Kosher Meat Upon Which God's Name Has Not Been Pronounced Permissible?
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadh Salman Younas, 19 November 2014. Supports: the Hanafi and Hanbali schools require God's name over each animal; the Shafi'i school holds it recommended; some Malikis hold it a condition only for Muslims; concludes kosher meat can be eaten, as most contemporary scholars have ruled.

title: Passport photo requirements
organization: Government of Canada (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, Passport Program)
label: Government of Canada
note: Page modified 23 September 2026. Supports: head coverings worn daily for religious or medical reasons are accepted if the full face is clearly visible and there are no shadows on the face; hair must be off the face so its edges are visible.

title: I cover my head or face for religious or cultural reasons. What will happen when I go to have my photo taken for biometrics?
label: Government of Canada
note: Page modified 1 September 2026. Supports: the whole face must be visible for the biometrics photo; you may ask for an operator of the same gender and a privacy curtain.

title: Official MTO Driver's Handbook: Getting your driver's licence
organization: Government of Ontario, Ministry of Transportation
label: Official source
note: Updated 14 September 2026. Supports: 'You can wear headwear for religious or medical reasons but it must not cover any part of your face.'

title: Renew your health card
label: Official source
note: Updated 21 September 2026. Supports: religious or medical headwear is allowed in the health card photo if it does not cover any part of the face.

title: Sunan an-Nasa'i 5148: Gold and silk for women, not men
label: Hadith reference
note: Sunan an-Nasa'i 5148, graded sahih (Darussalam). Cited for: gold and silk are permitted to the females of the Prophet's nation and forbidden to its males.

title: Sahih Muslim 2067a: Do not wear silk or brocade
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih Muslim. Cited for: do not drink from gold or silver vessels and do not wear brocade or silk. The chapter covers gold rings and silk for men.

title: Are Men Allowed to Wear Rings Made from Gold and Other Materials?
label: Scholar answer
note: Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam al-Kawthari (Darul Iftaa Leicester), republished on SeekersGuidance, 4 February 2011 (Hanafi, citing Radd al-Muhtar). Supports: white gold is gold; in the Hanafi school a man may wear only a silver ring under one mithqal in weight, and rings of other metals are not permitted. Other schools are not covered.

title: Is Rennet in Cheese Halal or Haram to Consume?
label: Scholar answer
note: Mawlana Ilyas Patel (Hanafi), 5 February 2011. Supports: in the Hanafi school rennet from animals other than pigs is permissible; because the schools differ, it is better to avoid rennet from an unknown source; check the label or ask the manufacturer.

title: Is Hunting Permissible?
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Abdul-Rahim Reasat, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 5 April 2021. Supports: hunting for food or income is permitted; hunting for sport is not (citing Sahih Muslim).

title: What Is the Ruling of Catch-and-Release Fishing?
label: Scholar answer
note: Mawlana Ilyas Patel (Hanafi), 18 June 2026. Supports: catch-and-release fishing is impermissible, even when done to sharpen skills; keep and eat a legal catch.

title: Is It Impermissible to Go to a Mixed Gym?
label: Scholar answer
note: Mawlana Ilyas Patel, checked by Shaykh Abdul-Rahim Reasat, 24 September 2024 (no school named). Supports: the God-conscious choice is to avoid mixed gyms; suggests a home gym, a training partner, quieter hours or a private area, and to keep looking for a men-only gym.

title: Going to a mixed gym (AMJA fatwa 23345)
organization: Assembly of Muslim Jurists of America (AMJA)
label: Scholar answer
note: Dr. Main Khalid Al-Qudah, 20 July 2008. Supports: a gym is like a supermarket or a street, so one can go, lower the gaze and keep interaction to what is necessary.

title: Is It Unlawful to Subscribe to Streaming Services?
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Irshaad Sedick, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 10 May 2022. Supports: subscribing to a streaming service is not direct assistance in sin; watching lawful content within reasonable limits is fine unless it leads to neglecting duties.

title: What is the Ruling on Photography in Islam?
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Dr. Muhammad Abu Bakr Badhib, 29 December 2024. Supports: contemporary scholars differ on photography; Baghithan permits it; al-Quda holds corrupting images prohibited and others better avoided, with educational and medical images permitted.

title: About photography (AMJA fatwa 22672)
organization: Assembly of Muslim Jurists of America (AMJA)
label: Scholar answer
note: Dr. Ibrahim Dremali, 27 November 2005. Supports: images for necessity, need or a recognised interest are permitted and all others are prohibited, camera photos included. It does not present this as a difference of opinion.

title: Posting personal photos on Facebook (AMJA fatwa 79414)
organization: Assembly of Muslim Jurists of America (AMJA)
label: Scholar answer
note: Dr. Salah Al-Sawy, 14 July 2009. Supports: posting personal photos publicly, especially of girls and women, is not permissible.

title: Can We Use Deodorants, Creams, and Perfumes That Contain Alcohol?
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Faraz Rabbani (Hanafi), 25 June 2011. Supports: non-wine (synthetic) alcohol is not ritually impure, so deodorants, creams and perfumes containing it are permitted for external use; it is more precautious to avoid them because of the difference of opinion, including Imam Muhammad's stricter view.

title: Ear and Nose Piercings for Women
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Faraz Rabbani (Hanafi), 7 September 2009. Supports: customary ear and nose piercings for women are permitted; other piercings, including ear piercings for men, are not.

title: The Fiqh of Hair Dyes
label: Scholar answer
note: Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam (Hanafi), 26 October 2010. Supports: dyeing grey hair is recommended; pure black dye for adornment is disputed (many Hanafi scholars hold it impermissible, Imam Abu Yusuf permits it, Mufti Taqi Usmani calls it disliked); hair dye does not affect wudu or ghusl.

title: Sahih Muslim 2102b: Change grey hair but avoid black
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih Muslim. Cited for: 'Change it with something, but avoid black.' The Sunnah.com chapter heading reads 'Black Dye Is Haram'.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 5376: Say bismillah, eat with the right hand
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih al-Bukhari. Cited for: mention Allah's name, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is nearest to you.

title: Quran 24:61: Greet one another when you enter houses
label: Quran source
note: Cited for: when you enter houses, greet one another with a greeting of peace from Allah. The English wording is a translation of the meaning, checked against The Clear Quran.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 6311: Wudu, the right side and a supplication before sleep
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih al-Bukhari. Cited for: make wudu before going to bed, lie on your right side and say the supplication the Prophet taught.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 3225: Angels do not enter a house with a picture
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih al-Bukhari. Cited for: angels do not enter a house in which there is a dog or a picture of a living creature.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 5950: The picture-makers
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih al-Bukhari. Cited for: the picture-makers will receive the severest punishment on the Day of Resurrection.

title: Ramadan and diabetes (health-care provider tools)
label: Public health source
note: Supports: a pre-Ramadan assessment 1 to 3 months before; the risk groups (very high risk must not fast, for example poorly controlled type 1, severe hypoglycemia in the last 3 months, recent DKA, dialysis, insulin-treated diabetes in pregnancy; high risk, including well-controlled type 1, should not fast; moderate and low risk can fast with medical advice); breaking the fast for documented hypoglycemia or symptomatic hyperglycemia, for vomiting, diarrhea or orthostasis in type 2, and for blood ketones above 0.6 mmol/L in type 1. Summarises the 2018 Diabetes Canada position statement. The page is written for clinicians and does not say whether glucose testing affects the fast. No page date shown.

title: Invalidators of fasting in medical treatments (Resolution 93 (1/10))
label: Scholar answer
note: Resolution 93 (1/10), 10th session, Jeddah, 28 June to 3 July 1997. Section First lists as not breaking the fast: eye and ear drops, nasal drops or spray if nothing is swallowed, sublingual tablets, dental work and mouthwash if nothing is swallowed, skin, muscle and vein injections other than nutritive fluids, oxygen, creams and patches. Section Second: a doctor should advise postponing treatment only when the delay does no harm. Section Third defers for further study bronchodilator inhalers, blood sampling and transfusion, cupping (hijama), dialysis, rectal items and surgery under general anaesthesia. It does not say that blood tests leave the fast intact.

title: Using asthma inhalers during the fasting hours of Ramadan (Fatwa 20480)
label: Scholar answer
note: Supports: using an asthma inhaler does not break the fast. Dated 8 April 2024.

title: The fiqh of fasting Ramadan according to the school of Imam Shafi'i
label: Scholar answer
note: By Shaykh Jamir D. Meah, 15 April 2022 (modified 2 March 2024), Shafi'i school. Supports: a non-Muslim who becomes Muslim does not make up the Ramadan days before conversion, and making up the day of conversion is sunnah, not obligatory; expiation (kaffarah) is only for intercourse, is two consecutive months, and is not due on the woman; inhalers break the fast but may be used out of necessity with a make-up day; eye drops do not break the fast; nasal solutions that reach the sinus cavity do.

title: Ramadan and eating disorders
label: Public health source
note: Article by Fareeha Jay RD, 6 April 2022, published with the BDA note that articles give the author's view. UK source, used for clinical framing only. Supports: fasting can make restriction look normal, hide disordered eating and lead to bingeing at iftar; an eating disorder is an illness and the exemption from fasting applies; people can take part in Ramadan in other ways and can involve an imam.

title: Contact NEDIC
organization: National Eating Disorder Information Centre (University Health Network)
label: Mental health support
note: Canada's national eating disorder helpline, a University Health Network program. Supports: toll-free 1-866-633-4220, Toronto 416-340-4156, email nedic@uhn.ca and live chat on nedic.ca. The page gives two different sets of Friday chat hours, so the site links to it for current hours instead of quoting them.

title: Government of Canada provides interest-free loans for students, effective April 1
label: Government of Canada
note: News release of 31 March 2023. Supports: interest on Canada Student Loans and Canada Apprentice Loans permanently eliminated from 1 April 2023; interest that built up before then is still owed; Quebec, the Northwest Territories and Nunavut are not in the federal program. It says nothing about provincial loans.

title: Pay back OSAP
label: Government of Ontario
note: Updated 5 May 2026. Supports: no interest on the federal part of an OSAP loan since 1 April 2023; interest is charged on the Ontario part, including during the six-month grace period. Only Ontario's terms were checked; other provinces set their own.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 1936: Expiation for intercourse during a Ramadan fast
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Fasting, hadith 1936, graded sahih by the collection. Cited for: the man who had intercourse while fasting in Ramadan was told the expiation: free a slave, or else fast two consecutive months, or else feed sixty poor people.

title: Sahih Muslim 1164: Six days of Shawwal
label: Hadith reference
note: Sahih Muslim 1164a (in-book reference Book 13, Hadith 264), narrated by Abu Ayyub al-Ansari. Cited for: fasting Ramadan and then six days of Shawwal is like fasting perpetually.

title: Jami at-Tirmidhi 747: Fasting on Mondays and Thursdays
label: Hadith reference
note: Jami at-Tirmidhi 747, narrated by Abu Hurairah, graded hasan (Darussalam) on Sunnah.com. Cited for: deeds are presented on Monday and Thursday, and the Prophet loved his deeds to be presented while he was fasting.

title: Sunan an-Nasa'i 2420: Fasting three days each month
label: Hadith reference
note: Sunan an-Nasa'i 2420, narrated by Jarir, graded sahih (Darussalam) on Sunnah.com. Cited for: fasting three days of each month is like fasting a lifetime, and the white days are the 13th, 14th and 15th.

title: Jami at-Tirmidhi 761: Fasting the 13th, 14th and 15th
label: Hadith reference
note: Jami at-Tirmidhi 761, narrated by Abu Dharr, graded hasan (Darussalam) on Sunnah.com. Cited for: if you fast three days of a month, fast the 13th, 14th and 15th.

title: When should a new Muslim pay zakat?
label: Scholar answer
note: By Shaykh Irshaad Sedick, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 25 November 2022, Shafi'i school. Supports: a new Muslim owes no zakat until a full lunar year has passed from the day they became Muslim, and owes none for the time before Islam.

title: Can you give zakat in advance? How to calculate and deduct advanced payments
label: Financial education
note: Supports: the majority of scholars allow paying zakat before the zakat date if the full amount is paid by then; monthly advance payments are deducted at the end of the zakat year; you must already own the nisab. The page describes a limit of no more than two years ahead as a restriction some scholars add, which NZF calls a safe precaution, not a general rule. No named scholar or reviewer is shown.

title: Is it permissible to give zakat to non-Muslims?
label: Scholar answer
note: By Shaykh Dr. Muhammad Abu Bakr Badhib, 22 December 2024. Supports: zakat may only be given to Muslims. He quotes Bahr al-Madhhab for this view from al-Shafi'i, Malik, Ahmad, Ishaq and Abu Thawr.

title: Can we accept charity from or give charity to non-Muslims?
label: Scholar answer
note: By Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 11 November 2023, Hanafi school. Supports: voluntary charity other than zakat is recommended for good causes, including non-Muslim causes; giving zakat to non-Muslims through the category of those whose hearts are to be reconciled is disputed and considered abrogated in the Hanafi school. The page cites that category as Quran 9:61; the verse listing zakat recipients is 9:60.

title: Jami at-Tirmidhi 658: Charity to relatives counts twice
label: Hadith reference
note: Jami at-Tirmidhi 658, graded sahih (Darussalam) on Sunnah.com. Cited for: charity to a poor person is one charity, and charity to a relative is two, charity and keeping ties. The narration opens with breaking the fast with dates.

title: Where do I give bank interest to get rid of it? (AMJA 4170)
organization: Assembly of Muslim Jurists of America (AMJA)
label: Scholar answer
note: By Dr. Salah al-Sawy, 14 October 2012. Supports: interest received is spent on public facilities; it may go to needy relatives but not to parents; move savings to an Islamic bank. US context.

title: Halal mutual funds and 401k (AMJA 1774)
organization: Assembly of Muslim Jurists of America (AMJA)
label: Scholar answer
note: By Dr. Hatem al-Haj, 7 November 2006, written for a US 401(k). Supports: taking part in an employer retirement plan is permissible, especially with a match; choose Islamic funds first, then stocks on an Islamic index, then the funds with the least prohibited involvement; avoid bonds; purify a share of earnings (his estimate is about 5 to 15 percent). Canadian plans are similar but not named.

title: Allowed percentage of questionable income in investing stocks (AMJA 2066)
organization: Assembly of Muslim Jurists of America (AMJA)
label: Scholar answer
note: By Dr. Main Khalid al-Qudah, 10 March 2006. Supports: investing through a screened fund is allowed if the prohibited share of profit is deducted and given away (purification).

title: Decisions and recommendations of AMJA's third annual convention
organization: Assembly of Muslim Jurists of America (AMJA)
label: Scholar answer
note: The insurance and credit card text comes from the Conclusions and Recommendations of the Session on Financial Investments in Islam, an imams' workshop held in Sacramento, 13 to 17 May 2005, which AMJA's third annual convention (21 to 25 July 2005) approved under Topic Six. Supports: commercial insurance is an invalid contract in principle; health insurance is allowed by need until an Islamic alternative exists; insurance that comes with a car purchase is overlooked and an independent insurance contract is allowed only by need; insurance provided by an employer is acceptable; government social insurance is acceptable. Holding a credit card whose contract has an interest clause is allowed by need, on conditions: pay in full, real need, no alternative, no cash advances except in necessity. The page does not address life insurance.

title: What is a Tax-Free Savings Account (TFSA)
label: Government of Canada
note: Modified 17 September 2026. Supports: a TFSA can hold cash and qualified investments such as stocks, bonds, mutual funds and ETFs, and income earned inside it is generally tax-free.

title: Contributions to the Canada Pension Plan
label: Government of Canada
note: Updated 3 August 2026. Supports: every person over 18 who works in Canada outside Quebec and earns more than $3,500 a year must contribute to the CPP; Quebec has the QPP. The page does not give an upper age.

title: Car insurance (AMJA 86975)
organization: Assembly of Muslim Jurists of America (AMJA)
label: Scholar answer
note: By Shaykh Jamaal Zarabozo, 17 June 2012, answering a question from the UK. Supports: scholars in the West 'seem to be in agreement' that the legal minimum of car insurance is permissible, because of the harm of going without it.

title: How credit cards work
label: Government of Canada
note: Modified 15 October 2025. Supports: federally regulated card issuers must give at least a 21-day interest-free grace period on new purchases; interest applies if the balance is not paid in full by the due date; cash advances have no grace period and charge interest from the day they are taken.

title: Buy now, pay later plans
label: Government of Canada
note: Modified 14 October 2025. Supports: plans can carry set-up and processing fees; after a missed payment the rate can rise, for example from 0 percent to 35 percent, applied either to the whole purchase from the original date or only to the remaining balance, depending on the agreement; risk of overspending.

title: Psychology of wealth: an Islamic perspective on personal finance
label: Scholar education
note: By Dr. Osman Umarji, published 1 July 2021, updated 30 July 2024. Supports: spending on family with good intention is charity; moderation in spending; charity as lasting wealth.

title: Quran 2:280: Giving a debtor in hardship time
label: Quran source
note: Cited for: a debtor in hardship is given time until things ease, and forgiving the debt as charity is better. The English wording is a translation of the meaning, checked against The Clear Quran, the default translation at this link.

title: Vacation fraud
label: Public safety source
note: Modified 16 January 2026. Supports: scammers offer free or discounted trips, ask for personal details and deposits, and deliver a poor trip or none. General travel fraud, not specific to pilgrimage.

title: Should Muslims in the north fast 23 hours a day?
label: Scholar answer
note: Article by Dr. Jasser Auda on the Fiqh Council of North America site, 7 November 2021 (updated 13 August 2026). One author's survey with his own proposal, not a collective resolution of the Council. Supports: the views that people fast from local dawn to sunset and make up days on shorter days if it is too hard; estimate by Makkah and Madinah; estimate by the nearest moderate region; latitude-based caps (45 or 48 degrees). He concludes that each Muslim weighs these views.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 2026: I'tikaf in the last ten days of Ramadan
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih al-Bukhari, graded sahih by the collection, narrated by Aisha. Cited for: the Prophet stayed in the masjid for worship (i'tikaf) in the last ten days of Ramadan until he died, and his wives did so after him.

title: Zakat on jewelry
label: Financial education
note: By Sheikh Nabil Khan, 25 July 2022. Supports: the Hanbali, Shafi'i and Maliki schools do not require zakat on women's jewellery that is worn; the official Hanafi view is that zakat is due on all gold and silver, including worn jewellery; NZF encourages paying as the cautious view. Includes a section on items that mix metals.

title: Line 34900: Donations and gifts
label: Government of Canada
note: Modified 6 July 2026. Supports: federal and provincial or territorial non-refundable tax credits for gifts to registered charities and other qualified donees, claimed on line 34900 (federal) and line 58969 (provincial), with details in Schedule 9 and Guide P113. The receipt rules in P113 were not checked.

title: Sahih Muslim 302: Do everything except intercourse
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih Muslim (Book of Menstruation). When some people would not eat with or live in the same house as a menstruating woman, the Prophet recited Quran 2:222 and said 'Do everything except intercourse', and he showed displeasure at cutting off all contact. Supports: only intercourse pauses during a period, and women are not isolated.

title: Sunan Abi Dawud 212: What is above the waist-wrapper
label: Hadith reference
note: Graded sahih by al-Albani on Sunnah.com. 'What is above the waist-wrapper is lawful for you' during menstruation, and eating with a menstruating woman. Supports: the basis of the majority view that asks for a barrier between the navel and the knee.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 302: Closeness during a period with a waist-wrapper
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih al-Bukhari. The Prophet had his wife put on a waist-wrapper (izar) and was close to her during her period. Supports: closeness during a period, with a barrier, as the majority teach.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 1927: Kissing and embracing while fasting
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih al-Bukhari. 'The Prophet used to kiss and embrace (his wives) while he was fasting, and he had more power to control his desires than any of you.' Supports: a kiss or embrace is not the act that breaks the fast.

title: What Type of Intimacy Is Permitted between a Husband and a Wife during Her Menstruation?
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Yusuf Weltch, 5 November 2023, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, Hanafi. Touching between the navel and the knee only over a barrier, other touching allowed; cites Abu Dawud and Quran 2:222. Supports the Hanafi position only; the Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali positions stated on the site rest on the standard school summaries and need a reviewer.

title: Quran 4:23: The women a man may never marry
label: Quran source
note: The Clear Quran translation by Dr. Mustafa Khattab. Lists the women a man may never marry: mothers, daughters, sisters, aunts, nieces, foster-mothers and foster-sisters, mothers-in-law, stepdaughters under his guardianship if he consummated the marriage with their mothers, and sons' wives. Supports: the mahram categories, including the consummation condition for step-relations. The English wording is a translation of the meaning.

title: Quran 24:31: The relatives a woman may show her adornment to
label: Quran source
note: The Clear Quran translation by Dr. Mustafa Khattab. Believing women lower their gaze, guard their chastity and show their adornment only to husbands, fathers, fathers-in-law, sons, stepsons, brothers, brothers' and sisters' sons, fellow women and others named in the verse. Supports: the male mahram relatives, and that brothers-in-law and cousins are not among them. The English wording is a translation of the meaning.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 5232: Care with a husband's relatives
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih al-Bukhari; the same report is in Jami at-Tirmidhi 1171, graded sahih (Darussalam). 'Beware of entering upon the ladies'; asked about the husband's relatives, the Prophet said 'The in-laws of the wife are death itself.' Supports: extra caution with a husband's relatives. That brothers-in-law are not mahram rests on Quran 4:23 and 24:31, not on this hadith alone.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 5233: No seclusion without a mahram
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih al-Bukhari. 'No man should stay with a lady in seclusion except in the presence of a Dhu-Muhram', and a man is told to go on Hajj with his wife. Supports: not being alone with a non-mahram.

title: Can a Non-Muslim Relative Be My Mahram?
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Abdul-Rahim Reasat, 5 March 2018, Hanafi. A mahram is anyone a woman may never marry, including a non-Muslim uncle. She may travel with and be alone with a non-Muslim mahram who is not morally corrupt, and she dresses in front of him as before unless impropriety is feared. Hanafi view only.

title: Is My Non-Muslim Father-in-Law My Mahram (Non-marriageable Kin)?
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Irshaad Sedick, 3 September 2023, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, Shafi'i. 'The status of a person as a mahram is not contingent upon their religious affiliation'; a non-Muslim father-in-law is mahram.

title: Is a Non-Biological Stepfather Considered a Mahram to a Convert If He Raised Her?
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Abdul-Rahim Reasat, 15 February 2026, Hanafi. A stepfather married to the mother who raised her is mahram even if not Muslim; mahram status does not make travel or being alone permissible where there are safety concerns, and the same applies to siblings. Quran 4:23 ties the step-relationship to consummation of the marriage with the mother, so the wording needs a reviewer.

title: Islam and the LGBT Question: Reframing the Narrative
label: Research education
note: Credited to Yaqeen Institute, based on a presentation by Dr. Carl Sharif El-Tobgui, published 7 October 2022 and updated 4 June 2026. It cites Mobeen Vaid's MuslimMatters article 'Can Islam Accommodate Homosexual Acts?' (11 July 2016). Supports: people are not morally responsible for same-sex attraction or gender dysphoria to the extent that they did not choose it; same-sex acts, and socially, chemically or surgically transitioning, are sinful; scholars differed on natural gender-atypical mannerisms; support should be private and given with clarity, compassion and conviction. The peer groups the paper names were not vetted and are not listed on this site.

title: Living with Same-Sex Attraction as a Muslim (Dogma Disrupted podcast)
label: Research education
note: Hosted by Imam Tom Facchine; the guest speaks under a pseudonym. Personal testimony that desires are part of a person, not the whole identity, and that support through mentorship, therapy and connection helps. Used for tone only, not for rulings.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 6243: The self wishes and desires
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih al-Bukhari. 'The adultery of the eyes is the sight ... the inner self wishes and desires and the private parts testify all this or deny it.' Supports: separating a desire from the act.

title: Quran 24:30: Lower the gaze and guard chastity
label: Quran source
note: The Clear Quran translation by Dr. Mustafa Khattab. 'Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their chastity. That is purer for them.' Supports: the basis for avoiding pornography. The English wording is a translation of the meaning.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 5066: Whoever cannot marry should fast
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih al-Bukhari. 'Whoever among you can marry, should marry, because it helps him lower his gaze and guard his modesty ... whoever is not able to marry, should fast.' Supports: fasting as help for someone who cannot marry yet.

title: Are Masturbation and Pornography Viewed Sinful by Different Schools of Thought?
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Yusuf Weltch, 29 July 2022, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani. Viewing pornography is prohibited in the relied-upon Hanafi and Shafi'i positions, and masturbation is strictly prohibited in both schools; deal with the habit directly rather than look for loopholes.

title: What Is the Ruling on Masturbation?
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Farid Dingle, 19 June 2022, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani. Says masturbation is forbidden and that the four Sunni schools agree, and that ghusl is needed if fluid comes out after orgasm. Its four-school agreement claim conflicts with the Hanbali necessity view reported by Islamweb fatwa 82271, so the site presents the difference instead.

title: Masturbation at the time of necessity (Fatwa 82271)
label: Scholar answer
note: 26 November 2001, answering a revert. In the Hanbali school masturbation is forbidden, and permissible only at necessity: fear of zina, or fear of illness, with inability to marry. Two reports from Imam Ahmad: that it is disliked, and that it is forbidden even when zina is feared. Advises avoiding obscene material, physical activity, good company and fasting.

title: Lowering the Gaze: Prophetic Solutions to Pornography in an Age of Endless Temptation
label: Research education
note: Dr. Jibran Khokhar, Yaqeen Senior Fellow and Canada Research Chair at Western University, published 27 August 2026 (Yaqeen labels it a blog). Supports: temptation is not itself evidence of weak faith; hope-based repentance; accountability software, removing triggering apps and placing devices in shared spaces; marriage is not a cure, and a spouse should never be expected to act as a therapist.

title: Sahih Muslim 1006: Reward in lawful intimacy
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih Muslim (Book of Zakat). 'In man's sexual intercourse (with his wife) there is a Sadaqa', with the reasoning that the unlawful act carries a burden and the lawful one a reward. Supports: lawful intimacy is good and rewarded.

title: Sunan Abi Dawud 2162: Anal intercourse is prohibited
label: Hadith reference
note: Graded hasan by al-Albani on Sunnah.com. 'He who has intercourse with his wife through her anus is accursed.' Supports: anal intercourse is prohibited.

title: Jami at-Tirmidhi 1165: Anal intercourse is prohibited
label: Hadith reference
note: Graded hasan (Darussalam) on Sunnah.com. 'Allah will not look at a man who enters a man or a woman in the behind.' Supports: anal intercourse is prohibited.

title: Sahih Muslim 1437a: Keeping a spouse's secrets
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih Muslim. Among the most wicked on the Day of Judgment is the man who goes to his wife and she to him, and then he spreads her secret. The wording is about the husband. Supports: privacy between spouses.

title: Marital Relations: The Legal Status of Oral and Other Forms of Sexual Gratification
label: Scholar answer
note: Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam, 1 June 2011, Hanafi. Two acts are clearly prohibited, anal intercourse and intercourse during menstruation, and spouses may give each other pleasure in other ways. Swallowing impure fluids is unlawful; oral contact without them is permissible though disliked, with a difference reported in Fatawa Hindiyya and most scholars holding it disliked. Hanafi view only; other schools need a reviewer.

title: Criminal Code s. 273.1: Meaning of consent
organization: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
label: Canadian law
note: Current to 3 September 2026. Consent is voluntary agreement to the sexual activity in question, it must be present at the time, and there is no consent where a person is unconscious or incapable, where trust, power or authority is abused, where lack of agreement is expressed, or where agreement is withdrawn. Information only, not legal advice.

title: Criminal Code s. 278: Spouse may be charged
organization: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
label: Canadian law
note: Current to 3 September 2026. 'A husband or wife may be charged with an offence under section 271, 272 or 273 in respect of his or her spouse, whether or not the spouses were living together'. Information only, not legal advice.

label: Support directory
note: Says to call 911 if you are in immediate danger, and lists sexual assault centres, crisis lines, shelters and transition houses by province and territory, with national lines including Hope for Wellness, Kids Help Phone and Trans Lifeline. Provincial numbers were not checked one by one.

title: Permissibility of these birth control methods! (AMJA fatwa 83665)
organization: Assembly of Muslim Jurists of America (AMJA)
label: Scholar answer
note: Dr. Hatem al-Haj, 31 January 2011. Fertility is a blessing and large families are encouraged; with a legitimate reason, such as the mother's weakness or inability to care for more children, birth control is allowable, not obligatory; cites Jabir on 'azl; consult a physician.

title: IUD for 5 and 8 years (AMJA fatwa 83770)
organization: Assembly of Muslim Jurists of America (AMJA)
label: Scholar answer
note: Dr. Hatem al-Haj, 13 February 2011. An IUD is permissible whenever birth control is indicated, and the duration of use does not matter; birth control is permissible, not obligatory.

title: The ruling of using birth control (Fatwa 6101)
label: Scholar answer
note: 30 July 2013. The schools almost agree that 'azl is permissible with the couple's mutual agreement, and neither may practise it without the other's agreement; birth control as a permanent means of ending the possibility of conception contradicts Islam. No necessity exception is stated for permanent methods.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 5208 and 5209: Withdrawal ('azl) while the Quran was revealed
label: Hadith reference
note: In Sahih al-Bukhari; Sunnah.com serves 5208 and 5209 as one combined entry, and Sahih Muslim 1440a has the same report. Jabir said the companions practised withdrawal ('azl) while the Quran was being revealed. Supports: the classical basis for temporary contraception.

label: Health information
note: Summaries of contraceptive methods and the It's a Plan tool, with advice to talk choices over with a health care provider. Health information, not religious guidance.

title: Quran 4:3: Up to four, or one if you fear injustice
label: Quran source
note: The Clear Quran translation by Dr. Mustafa Khattab. 'marry other women of your choice, two, three, or four. But if you are afraid you will fail to maintain justice, then (content yourselves with) one'. Supports: the permission and its condition of justice. The English wording is a translation of the meaning.

title: Quran 4:129: Full fairness between wives is not possible
label: Quran source
note: The Clear Quran translation by Dr. Mustafa Khattab. 'You will never be able to maintain (emotional) justice between your wives, no matter how keen you are.' The English wording is a translation of the meaning.

Up to five years on indictment. Information only, not legal advice.

title: Sunan Ibn Majah 2045: What people are forced to do is forgiven
label: Hadith reference
note: Graded sahih (Darussalam) on Sunnah.com. 'Allah has forgiven my nation for mistakes and forgetfulness, and what they are forced to do.' Supports: a person forced into something carries no sin for it.

title: Do Four Witnesses Apply to Proving Sexual Assault?
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 9 June 2026, Hanafi. 'A woman who is assaulted bears no sin whatsoever, for coercion lifts accountability'; the four-witness rule is for convicting zina and is not a burden on the victim; involve family, the authorities and a counsellor.

title: Was My Childhood Sexual Abuse Due to Allah Punishing Me?
label: Scholar answer
note: Ustadha Shazia Ahmad, 12 January 2025. On childhood abuse: no child is abused because Allah is punishing them, the perpetrator is accountable, and therapy is encouraged alongside dua. Cited only for 'abuse is not a punishment'.

title: Sexual and reproductive health
label: Health information
note: Page modified 27 August 2025. Links to guidance on getting tested for sexually transmitted infections: when to test, where to go and types of testing. The detail page was not opened. Health information, not religious guidance.

title: Sunan Ibn Majah 1920: Cover your awrah except from your wife
label: Hadith reference
note: Graded hasan (Darussalam) on Sunnah.com. 'Cover your awrah, except from your wife and those whom your right hand possesses'; when alone, 'Allah is more deserving that you should feel shy before Him'. Supports: no awrah between spouses, and modesty when alone.

title: Quran 2:256: No compulsion in religion
label: Quran source
note: Cited for: there is no compulsion in religion, so nobody should be pressured into becoming Muslim. The English wording is a translation of the meaning (Saheeh International).

title: Quran 28:56: Guidance is from Allah
label: Quran source
note: Cited for: the Prophet could not guide even those he loved; guidance is from Allah, so nobody can make another person believe. The English wording is a translation of the meaning (Saheeh International).

title: Is It Wrong To Delay Someone's Shahada?
label: Scholar answer
note: Shaykh Abdul-Rahim Reasat, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 6 May 2022. Supports: faith (iman) is affirmation in the heart, so 'the person who turns up to say the shahada is already a Believer'; the spoken Shahada is what lets the community apply worldly rulings. This is one of three scholarly positions (see the Salman Younas answer).

title: Making Up Missed Prayers: I Believed but Did Not Utter the Testimony of Faith
label: Scholar answer
note: Salman Younas, checked by Faraz Rabbani, 8 April 2010. Supports: three scholarly positions on the spoken Shahada: a condition of faith, a part of faith, or a condition only for worldly rulings. The answer says all three positions are strong and advises the cautious approach of making up prayers missed between believing and saying it.

title: Why Islam Canada: free Quran and brochures
label: Official organization
note: Supports: a free English Quran translation and five brochures with 'no commitment', and a 'Talk To A Rep' web contact route, run by ICNA Canada in Oakville, Ontario. No phone number is shown. Orders are fulfilled by ICNA Canada and GainPeace.org, and the order form asks for a full street address (no PO boxes).

The site footer says that giving your contact information is consent to email, SMS, phone and postal communications.
